content.canDo: After this you can buy something at a corner shop, ask what it costs and hand over the money without switching to English.
content.intro: Buying at a despensa is a fixed little exchange, and it starts with the shopkeeper, not you: '¿Qué te doy?' is the Paraguayan opening, and it uses vos, so the verb is 'doy' + 'te'. Two traps for English speakers: prices are said in thousands ('diez mil', not 'ten thousand guaranies'), and 'dame' sounds blunt in English but is completely normal here — softening it with 'por favor' is all you need.

vocab.note: The shopkeeper opens with this. Literally 'what do I give you' — the vos form.
'Dame' is the normal way to order. It is not rude.
Guaraníes are always said in thousands. Nobody says the currency out loud.
'Tenés' is the vos form of tener — never 'tienes' here.

lines.gloss: Say beef, and ask what it comes to.

You are at the despensa and want a cold bottle of water and a packet of biscuits. Order both, then ask what it comes to.
